body: Sync: in step on the owner's rules (three games by popularity, subagents, slot caps, branch reviews). Three shared items are still in flight: BewareILive's port of hooks 8d77ed9 (i-codex-broker-leak), its copy of #42, and our sync-check branch, which lists 16 shared-path drifts and 3 decisions to reconcile; it lands after Tempest and Battlezone. Context7: not enough. Across today's 56 VectorCraft transcripts there were 28 lookups, all in the main session and mostly for the statusline; subagents made none, although they write MAME Lua all day. Fix: name the lookup as a required first step in each agent prompt (MAME Lua API before any new tap or call), and have the subagent hook check for it. Speed: building isn't the bottleneck, landing is. One branch at a time goes through rebase, a gate on every commit and a review, and baseline branches conflict on the shared docs/mechanics.md and parity-checklist.md, so every landing forces the next one to rebase. Proposals: (1) split mechanics.md and the oracle manifest per game (#45), which removes most rebase conflicts; (2) baseline branches that touch only their game's files gate on the docs-only path; (3) batch small shared-tool requests into one agent (done for dump.lua now). Tokens: (a) use Sonnet or Haiku agents for mechanical work (regens, reflows, prose passes, conflict resolution, OCR reading) and keep Opus for specs, challenges and oracle work; (b) shorter prompts that point at facts sheets instead of repeating rules; (c) a 60-minute check-in when nothing has landed; (d) the main session stops reading agent outputs and full docs and works from their final reports. Owner decisions here: (a) and (c), and whether to start (1) before the next landings.
summary: VectorCraft on sync, process, tokens and Context7: in step on rules, three ports pending; landing is the bottleneck; subagents made no Context7 lookups today
